newsitem.title: USA: Marvel bondholders win battle for company.
newsitem.headline: Marvel bondholders win battle for company.

text.p: Marvel Entertainment Group Inc.'s bondholders, capping a long-fought battle for control of the bankrupt comic book publisher, said Friday they seized the company's board and named investor Carl Icahn as its chairman.

The move was made possible by a bankruptcy court judge's ruling earlier in the day to reject a request by Marvel's banks and management -- led by financier Ronald Perelman -- for an emergency order to block the bondholders.

Marvel's banks and management have been battling the bondholders for control of the company, whose titles include Spiderman and the Incredible Hulk, since it declared Chapter 11 bankruptcy last December.
"We won the company, now we're going to fix it," said a person close to the bondholders, who declined to be named.
The bondholders said now they would bring in a transition team led by former Marvel executive Joseph Calamari to lead the company back to financial health.
They also said they ousted the board of Toy Biz, whose shares are more than 70.0 percent owned by Marvel. They said they named Icahn to Toy Biz's board as well.

Since the bondholders owned 80.0 percent of the Marvel stock that secured their bonds, they used the stock's voting rights to oust the company's present board. The shares secured nearly $900 million in debt.
Officials from Marvel were not immediately available to comment.
